speedrun: cat /app/config/config.yaml  # get key_id and HMAC key
xxd /app/data/logs/$(ls /app/data/logs/ | head -1) | head -8  # confirm file format: 4B key_id + 16B nonce + 4B len + ciphertext
bash /app/selftest.sh  # get known plaintext->ciphertext hex pairs for multiple key_ids
python3 -c "import binascii; ct=bytes.fromhex('<ciphertext>'); pt=b'<known_64_byte_plaintext>'; print(binascii.hexlify(bytes(a^b for a,b in zip(ct,pt))))"  # recover 64 keystream bytes
nm /app/lib/encryptor.so  # check exported and internal symbol names for LFSR hints
objdump -d /app/lib/encryptor.so > /tmp/disasm.txt && grep -A5 -B5 'shr\|xor\|and' /tmp/disasm.txt | head -100  # find LFSR feedback logic
# Identify Galois LFSR: tap mask 0x80200003, seed = key_id XOR crc32_ieee(nonce), 1 LSB per step, 8 steps per byte
# Verify: reimplement LFSR in Python, check against recovered keystream bytes
python3 -c "<LFSR verification script comparing computed vs recovered keystream>"
go run /app/tools/decrypt/main.go /app/data/logs/$(ls /app/data/logs/ | head -1)  # check LOG_ENTRY: prefix
go run /app/tools/decrypt/main.go /app/data/logs/$(ls /app/data/logs/ | sed -n '100p')  # spot check another file
# Manually verify HMAC on one file to confirm correctness
# Test on a long entry if available in corpus
strace -e trace=openat go run /app/tools/decrypt/main.go /app/data/logs/$(ls /app/data/logs/ | head -1) 2>&1 | grep encryptor  # confirm no .so open
invalid_failure_risks: CRC32 variant unspecified: Go has IEEE, Castagnoli, Koopman variants; blueprint says 'crc32(nonce)' without specifying which. Agent using wrong variant fails all verify-time inputs with no clear diagnostic.

Dual output behavior underspecified: instruction says tool writes to stdout AND to /app/verify/outputs/<filename>.txt, but doesn't clarify whether this is always done or only when input path contains 'verify/inputs'. Agent may write output files only when explicitly invoked differently, or always, causing path collisions.

golang-1.22 package name: on Debian bookworm the package is 'golang-1.22' but the go binary path may be /usr/lib/go-1.22/bin/go, not in PATH by default. Could cause 'go build' failures unrelated to the task.
strace check on 'go run' is noisy: go run opens many files during compilation; the check needs to filter carefully or use a pre-built binary. A false positive could invalidate a correct solution.

selftest binary path not specified in instruction: agent must discover whether to run '/app/service --selftest' or 'go run /app/main.go --selftest'; if the service binary isn't pre-compiled, this adds a step.

Tap mask endianness/form: the blueprint states 0x80200003 as the Galois feedback mask, but the disassembly may show it differently depending on compiler optimization. An agent reading the disassembly might reconstruct a different mask.

File format offset ambiguity: blueprint says '4 bytes key_id (LE) + 16 bytes nonce + 4 bytes plaintext_len (LE) + N bytes ciphertext' but the instruction draft says 'nonce (16 bytes) and key_id (4 bytes, little-endian) are prepended... followed by a 4-byte little-endian plaintext length'. The order (key_id first vs nonce first) is inconsistent between the two descriptions.
review.reasons: The blueprint has a critical internal inconsistency: the environment spec says the file format is 'key_id (4B) + nonce (16B) + len (4B) + ciphertext' but the cipher description says 'nonce and key_id are prepended' implying nonce-first order. This ambiguity would cause an agent to fail for reasons unrelated to skill. Additionally, the CRC32 variant is unspecified, which is a silent correctness trap that constitutes an invalid failure mode rather than a genuine difficulty. The dual-output behavior (stdout AND file write) is underspecified in the instruction draft.
fixes: Resolve file format order inconsistency: explicitly state in both the instruction and environment spec that the format is key_id(4B LE) + nonce(16B) + plaintext_len(4B LE) + ciphertext(N bytes), with no contradicting description.
Specify CRC32 variant explicitly: state 'IEEE CRC32 (Go hash/crc32.ChecksumIEEE / polynomial 0xEDB88320)' in the environment spec so the agent has an unambiguous target.

Clarify dual output behavior: either (a) make the tool always write to /app/verify/outputs/ when the input path is under /app/verify/inputs/ (and document this), or (b) give the tool a --output flag, or (c) have the verifier run the tool with a redirect. The current instruction implies both stdout and file output simultaneously without explaining the mechanism.
Specify the selftest binary invocation path explicitly (e.g., '/app/bin/service --selftest' or 'go run /app/main.go --selftest') so the agent doesn't waste commands discovering it.
Fix the strace check to operate on a pre-built binary rather than 'go run' to avoid false positives from Go toolchain file opens.
